resources.string: No web-session AI accounts. Add one from the AIs tab in the Kripton Code window.
The desktop is empty. Open an AI or an app from the button at the bottom left.
This AI is currently used by a run.
Browsing files and dropping them into AI windows needs Android’s “all files access” permission. A file is handed to a window’s web page only when you drop it there; it is not sent anywhere else.
Long-press a file and drag it onto an AI window, or send it from the row menu.
No AI window is open. Open one first.
The file could not be read, or a folder was dropped
The %1$s page is not ready yet
The chosen app opens next to Kripton Code using Android split screen.
Split screen looks off. Open Kripton Code in “Split screen” from Recents, then start the app from here.

Desktop mode runs full screen; system bars appear briefly when you swipe from the edge. The Files window asks for all-files access; grant it now or the first time you open Files. The side-by-side list reads the names of installed apps. Nothing leaves the device on its own.
Full screen, draggable windows, a taskbar and a file manager. Once turned on the app always starts in this mode; turn it off here or from the taskbar.
This mode is for tablets (short screen side of at least 600 dp).

The app becomes a full-screen windowed desktop: AI web UIs move and resize like simple windows, and files are dropped onto an AI by drag and drop. Once on, every launch starts in this mode; you can turn it off any time.
The app will start with the normal view next time. You can turn desktop mode back on from Settings or the side menu.
